abstract: Insects rely on chemosensory cues to mediate essential behaviors, including mate recognition. In Drosophila melanogaster, the odorant receptor OR67d detects the male-specific pheromone cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA), initiating diverse behavioral responses. However, the evolutionary conservation and functional tuning of OR67d receptors across Drosophila species remain largely unexplored. Here, we characterize OR67d receptors from nine Drosophila species using phylogenetic analysis, transgenic expression, and electrophysiology. While most orthologs retained sensitivity to cVA, some exhibited broader tuning, responding to structurally similar acetates. Notably, D. bipectinata and D. navojoa responded to cVA despite not producing it, raising the possibility that cVA detection has been maintained independently of endogenous production, possibly as a heterospecific cue. Structural modeling revealed overall high sequence conservation yet identified variable regions within the putative binding pocket potentially underlying differences in ligand selectivity. These findings contribute to our understanding of pheromone receptor evolution and how chemical communication systems diversify across Drosophila species.
